title: Ferdinand and Isabella to Rodrigo González de Puebla, Almazán, 21 June 1496, ciphered article, AGS Patronato Real leg. 52 doc. 47 f. 396 (catalogue 616)

documents.shelfmark: AGS, Patronato Real, leg. 52, doc. 47, ff. 396r-396v (old stamp T.c.Y.2; PARES description 2207769, images 5-6)

plaintext.source: The minuta of 21 June 1496 carries the article in clear (note on f. 397v; closing leaves ff. 398r-399r in the same unit); Bergenroth, CSP Spain I (1862) no. 138, pp. 106-107, abstracts it and quotes the opening; no. 137 abstracts the draft.

transcription.source: PARES show/2207769, image 5 (f. 396r heading and lines 1-3 only)
transcription.notes: Sample only. Line 2 group corrected in the check to DCCCCXXI (wide ligature with overbar). Image 5 at the largest size PARES serves, 1005 x 1402 px.

system.summary: Puebla's Great Roman Numeral code: an alphabetical one-part code of words and names numbered in Roman figures (key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33), mixed with clear words.

diacritics.note: C ligatures: plain = CC, with a superscript o = CCC, wide with an overbar = CCCC (read on key images 48, 51-53, 101, 110, 116).

system.sibling_key: Same code and key as targets/puebla1495 (catalogue 615). Key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33, PARES show/2207755.
system.notes: Tomokiyo's note that CC and CCC are written in ligature does not settle the count; the superscript o and the overbar do.

prior_solution.where: Bergenroth, CSP Spain I (1862) nos. 137-138, pp. 104-107; the minuta in the same unit (contemporary clear text)

conditions.human_role: WAINUT: the owner set the task (catalogue items 615-617). The work was done by AI language-model agents, and a second agent re-checked it on the images and the key. No human reading.
tools: decode_sample.py (key-excerpt lookup; shift, ligature and shuffle controls)
models: AI language-model agents (WAINUT; versions not recorded here)

solution.what: PARES show/2207769: 12 images, ff. 394r-399v; contents mapped (two clear drafts, the cipher leaf, 19th-century notes).
CSP Spain I (BHO): no. 138 quotes the opening of the ciphered article word for word; no. 137 = the draft of 21 June 1496; no. 141 = the draft of 6 July 1496.
First pass with Tomokiyo's published values: six groups (que, Rey de Inglaterra, Escocia, nuestros, de, De Puebla) fit the quotation; C-count left open.
Key AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 33 read on images 30, 37, 48, 50-54, 100-101, 110, 116: C-count rule for the three ligature forms; 921 = el Rey de Escocia, 922 = el Reyno de Escocia.
decode_sample.py: key shifted by -1, +1, -7, +13 entries, every ligature read as CC, and three shuffles of the groups: none gives the quoted sentence.
Second agent re-read the heading and lines 1-3 on fresh crops and the f. 397v note; line 2 group corrected from 'Escocia' to DCCCCXXI 'el Rey de Escocia'.

outcome.method_basis: The article was deciphered at the time (the minuta carries it in clear, note on f. 397v) and Bergenroth calendared it (CSP Spain I no. 138); the extant key was applied here only to a sample, which matches his quotation group for group, except that the cipher has 'el Rey de Escocia' where he has 'Escocia'.
outcome.notes: The key state is 'recovered' because the whole key survives in the archive; only the entries in key_excerpt.tsv were looked up. Proposed: catalogue 616 becomes an earlier-solution pointer to CSP Spain I no. 138 (with nos. 137 and 141 for the drafts in the same unit), dated Almazán, 21 June 1496.

texts.label: AGS PTR leg. 52 doc. 47 f. 396r, sample (heading and lines 1-3)
texts.summary: Ferdinand and Isabella answer De Puebla's report that Henry VII had good news of the affairs of the King of Scots: the news comes from nowhere but their own envoys sent to Scotland (Bergenroth's no. 137: the Spanish ambassadors obtained a solemn promise from the King of Scots).

reading_review.note: The heading and lines 1-2 read as sentences and match Bergenroth's quotation; line 3 is doubtful and marked.
